items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: And also Rosa Hart from Lake Charles, who has gone on.

ctx.x: So they got in touch with Mr. Gastel', my manager, and told him what they wanted. Well, he knew the whole story. My family knew the whole story, and my little sister Vida, who

used to travel with me, I told you about her. Vida was instrumental, and another friend who has gone on also. Vida has gone on, of course, and this friend Eugenia. Well, they got together and got all these facts, and we have a darling little friend back in Louisiana, Mary -- what's her name? Mary Burn Elliott. And also Rosa Hart from Lake Charles, who has gone on. But Rosa Hart was very, very strong and very instrumental in keeping the little theater going in Lake Charles, you know.

But anyway, anything theatrical and anybody theatrical she was with it and for it. She was just a marvelous person and Mary Burn Elliott and her family were just tremendous. So they knew all of this was going on, and they did the works of getting this thing, putting it in action. Unbeknownst to me, you know, and I absolutely had no idea, really. Because I've had people ask me, "You mean to tell me you didn't know?" I say no, I did not know. I had seen the show, you know, but I -- the way it was put to me, and…
